clue.text: Seen rebuilding, united internally, Germany succeeded

indicators.note: rebuilding means putting the parts together again in a new order
something placed internally goes inside the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written
U is the standard abbreviation for united
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: Germany's postwar reconstruction after reunification, seen as a success story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Germany succeeded' reads as a historical verdict, but the country is only a one-letter vehicle code, and the verb on the end is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow on in sequence, just as one thing succeeded another by coming after it.

clue.text: Starts to inculcate new habits and use latest excellent rope - this one?

definitions.text: Starts to inculcate new habits and use latest excellent rope - this one?

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their opening letters, one from each

blocks.clueFragment: inculcate new habits and use latest excellent rope
blocks.note: the first letter of each of these eight words

explanation.surface: A sailing instructor trying to drill good habits into a crew about using the best rope.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the initials spell the answer, and the clue as a whole describes a rope that sailors learn to use.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhauler is a sailing line used for hauling a sail or boom inward, so it is the kind of rope the clue asks about.

clue.text: The wild disposition

blocks.note: first meaning: the natural world untouched by people
second meaning: a person's basic character or temperament

explanation.walkthrough: Read together, the clue sounds like an untamed temperament, but the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the natural world of plants and animals and someone's inborn character or temperament.

clue.text: Pile inexpensive when roofless!

indicators.note: in a down entry the roof is the top letter, so losing it means dropping the first letter

blocks.note: a synonym

explanation.surface: An exclamation about cheap housing: a pile of a place, bargain-priced because it has no roof.
explanation.walkthrough: CHEAP loses its top letter C, leaving HEAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A heap is an untidy stack of things, which is a common synonym for a pile.

clue.text: In from France, reluctant to be seen in Church cover

indicators.note: a word seen in another sits inside it, so these letters go within the next ones

blocks.note: en is French for in
loth is a variant spelling of loath, unwilling
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A French visitor shy about being seen inside a church, perhaps looking for some cover.
explanation.walkthrough: Loth is the older spelling of loath, still common in crosswords; the church abbreviation is split around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To enclothe is to dress or clothe someone, which is to cover them with garments.

clue.text: Quickly enter Irish game associated with Physical Training

blocks.note: IR is a standard abbreviation for Irish

the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: An Irish sport linked with PE lessons at school.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrupt is to burst or rush suddenly into a place, so it means entering quickly and forcibly.

clue.text: Fighter ran with a stick raised

blocks.note: tore along means ran fast
taken as written
a synonym

explanation.surface: A combatant charged forward brandishing a stick held high.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a raised weapon, but 'raised' turns only the stick upside down; the A stays as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: A toreador is a bullfighter, especially one on horseback, so he is a kind of fighter.

clue.text: Sadly untrained, not seeing river flood

indicators.note: something going sadly goes wrong, so the letters end up out of order
not seeing something means leaving it out of the word

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the usual abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Untrained people failing to notice a river until it bursts its banks.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the R from UNTRAINED, then rearrange the remaining eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To inundate is to overwhelm with water, the verb sense of flood.

clue.text: Lacking vision, managed in wrong way: dispute follows

blocks.note: ran a business means managed it
a row is a quarrel

clue.text: Country workers’ group have high opinion of, when finishing early

clue.text: Producer of filth? River, lakes - unfortunately true

blocks.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
L is the abbreviation for lake, doubled for the plural
taken as written

explanation.surface: An environmental complaint: rivers and lakes really are being dirtied by someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A polluter is one who contaminates the environment, so the question mark gives a playful description of someone making dirt.

clue.text: Loved one not working, you say?

blocks.note: idle means not working, and it is pronounced the same as the answer

explanation.surface: A question about a beloved person who never does any work.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is someone greatly adored or worshipped, a loved one in the sense of an object of devotion.

clue.text: Cite tax due - amazing precision

blocks.note: taken as written

clue.text: Lots of money needed by cashier - he’s forward-looking

a bank teller handles cash

explanation.definitionFit: A fortune-teller claims to predict what lies ahead, so he looks forward in time quite literally.

clue.text: Strand crowd drinking mineral

ore is rock containing minerals

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers on a beach crowding round to drink mineral water.

explanation.definitionFit: A forelock is a lock of hair growing over the forehead, so a single strand or tress of hair.

clue.text: Work Ben undid without being asked

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Unbidden means uninvited or spontaneous, done when nobody requested it.

clue.text: Resembling 14 after central character left - pleasing

the answer to 14 down

clue.text: Keynotes of his life primarily revealing statesman

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of these four words

the first and last letters
the definite article
